assertions.description: navigator.gpu is exposed — the object carrying the WGSL language-feature registry this feature is detected through.
navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures is a setlike with a has() method — the adapter-free detection surface for language features.
The buffer_view language feature is present in wgslLanguageFeatures (Chrome 153 developer trial).

A shader beginning with `requires buffer_view;` compiles exactly when the registry advertises the feature: rejected with a compilation error when absent, accepted when present. Skipped (false) when no GPU adapter is reachable — the manual assertion covers that case.
assertions.test: (async()=>{ if (!navigator.gpu) return false; const supported = navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures.has('buffer_view'); const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter(); if (!adapter) return false; const device = await adapter.requestDevice(); device.pushErrorScope('validation'); const mod = device.createShaderModule({ code: 'requires buffer_view;\n@compute @workgroup_size(1) fn m() {}' }); const info = await mod.getCompilationInfo(); const scopeErr = await device.popErrorScope(); const failed = info.messages.some((m) => m.type === 'error') || !!scopeErr; return failed === !supported; })()

assertions.description: On hardware with a real adapter, the registry claim and actual compilation must agree (no advertised-but-broken or working-but-unadvertised state).
assertions.test: Requires a machine with a usable GPU adapter: run the requires-directive lab and confirm its outcome matches the registry page's buffer_view entry.
